Invariant holds on 64k configs (2 clients, depth 9) and 22k (3 clients, depth 7) incl. arbitrary env ticks; Inv.mutex proven
Invariant does not need FIFO: the non-FIFO case (acquire h while h still holder) is absorbed by a+qn=w. Suggests many BEAM protocols are FIFO-agnostic for safety
nodes.description: While designing the numeric token invariant I expected to need Step.prefix (FIFO). Instead the a+qn=w equation handles the out-of-order case. FIFO matters for liveness (the token is not lost), not for mutual exclusion.

nodes.title: Prove Inv preserved by every Step via Step.chars + omega case analysis
Inv.step proven: ~450 lines, zero sorry. Client half ~150 lines, server half ~250. Every case is Step.chars + simp on singleton counts + omega
Proof cost driver was not the protocol but Lean plumbing: if-then-else on pids, singleton List.count, and subst renaming. A tactic that normalises Step.chars output would cut the proof in half
nodes.description: Errors across iterations: by_contra missing (no Mathlib), cases pattern arity, subst replacing a def-valued pid, List.count on singletons not reduced by default simp, match on srv catch-all not reducing without cases on the Option. None were about the invariant, which the bounded model check had already validated.

nodes.title: Add EnvStep/ReachEnv (ticks at any time), Inv (initCfg n), end-to-end mutex_forever theorem

Write elixir/lock.exs: same protocol on BEAM, random ticks, event-log overlap check
5 clients/2000 ticks and 20 clients/20000 ticks: max 1 holder, 0 violations
Mutation test: break the release-sender check in beh and confirm the bounded checker finds a violating trace
Grant-while-held caught at 279 configs, duplicate-acquire (token loss, mutex still holds) caught at 59 via Inv, no-sender-check unreachable: identical 64303-config state space

The invariant is stronger than the property: it catches the lost-token bug that mutual exclusion alone misses, and it identifies which defensive checks are load-bearing (none of the sender checks are, with honest clients)
nodes.description: First two mutants I wrote (no sender check on release; release on any message while holding) were both unreachable under honest clients and explored the same state space as the original. The invariant predicted this: r c p = 0 for non-holders, and no grant reaches a holding client. Replaced with grant-while-held (mutex violation) and duplicate-acquire (Inv violation only).

Refactor core: Behavior σ μ := Pid → σ → μ → σ × sends (self pid); drop me from Lock client state; re-prove
Refactor done in one build: Behavior is Pid -> σ -> μ -> ...; Lock proof lost the cli field and ~20 lines; all examples and mutants unchanged in output
Write elixir/to_lean.exs: parse @type + handle_cast/handle_info clauses into Lean inductives and a Behavior
to_lean.exs (~330 lines) translates lock.ex and bank.ex; generated Lean compiles; drivers run the same sources on BEAM

The @type declarations were sufficient as the type oracle: Option wrapping, none/nil, list cons, enum atoms, and the non-linear pattern {p, [n|rest]} all resolved from types alone. No @spec needed beyond msg/state
nodes.description: Type-directed decisions in the translator: variable at Option position already bound at base type -> some x' with guard; nil at Option -> none; atom at enum type -> constructor; {:noreply, v} with v : Int at Option Int -> some v. Guards become if-then-else with fallthrough to the next subsuming clause; subsumed clauses are dropped since Lean rejects redundant alternatives.

The equivalence proof was one line per model. Guard orientation (p = p') and clause order were the only things that had to match; field names and redundant catch-alls did not matter
Progress: a waiting client is never stuck; either some actor can step or someone is in the critical section waiting on the environment
Full liveness under fair scheduling with a ranking function
Deadlock freedom as a safety property derived from Inv, strengthened with holder=none -> queue=[]
Deadlock freedom from Inv; full liveness deferred (needs fairness machinery, no Mathlib)
Add queue_empty field to Inv, prove Enabled-or-holding theorem and mcount_pos -> Step exists
progress + progress_forever proven in ~50 lines using only Inv (plus the new queue_empty field). No FIFO needed here either

For this protocol FIFO is not needed for safety or deadlock freedom. It would only matter for a fairness argument (bounded waiting), which needs a ranking function and a fair scheduler. Step.prefix exists but is unused by any example
nodes.description: Earlier I predicted FIFO would be needed for liveness. The deadlock-freedom proof went through with Inv alone. The invariant's a+qn=w equation absorbs message reordering. Bounded waiting (a queued client is granted within k releases) is where queue order and hence FIFO would enter.

Await states are generated St constructors carrying the continuation's free variables; the reply type is a single shared Msg.reply. Limits: one @type reply per program, call must be an assignment statement, continuation cannot itself block (no nested awaits yet)

Nested/second blocking calls in the continuation would need recursion into plain_body with a fresh await index; not implemented. Also 'from' is a Lean keyword: added lean_ident sanitizer.

The rework was mechanical: three client shapes instead of two phases, reply .ok instead of grant, and the deferral clause is a frame case (popped message re-sent to self does not touch any counted message).

nodes.title: Bounded waiting / FCFS: a client queued at rank k acquires the lock after exactly k handovers; FIFO becomes load-bearing
Full liveness with a fair scheduler and ranking function
FCFS as a trace-safety property: rank decreases by exactly one per handover while queued; needs 'holder never queued', which needs mailbox order (release h precedes acquire h)
FCFS via two new Inv fields: ordered (no acquire h before release h in server mailbox) and holder_not_queued; plus a Waiting trace relation counting transfers
Count.lean: exact mailbox equations (mboxOf_deliverAll_eq, sendsTo) and mailbox clause in Step.chars

Count.lean: sendsTo, mboxOf_deliverAll_eq, mcount_eq_of_mboxOf; Step.chars now also gives the exact mailbox equation. Lock.lean: relBeforeAcq with tail/head/append lemmas, two new Inv fields; model check clean on 77925/23281 configs
LockProof: preserve ordered and holder_not_queued in every case; the A2 case (acquire h while h holds) closes only via relBeforeAcq_head

LockProof preserves ordered and holder_not_queued in all cases; the A2 case closed via relBeforeAcq_head + token arithmetic. LockFcfs: Step.rank_step, Waiting relation (steps + env), bounded_waiting, fcfs. Zero sorry, zero warnings, chain passes

FIFO is finally load-bearing, and in exactly the place predicted three sessions ago: the reorder 'acquire h while h holds' is harmless for safety and deadlock freedom but breaks rank accounting. The proof that excludes it uses only the tail-append shape of Step.chars' mailbox clause
nodes.description: The ordered field is an invariant over the server's mailbox *list*, not counts. Preservation needed exact mailbox equations (mboxOf_deliverAll_eq) rather than mcount. The general append lemma relBeforeAcq_append handles every send with one side condition: appending release h requires no pending acquire h, which follows from hd=1 -> a=0 in the token invariant.

nodes.title: Timers and remote exit signals: send_after / GenServer timeouts / Process.exit(pid, reason), with a watchdog example proven

Timers as a pending list; a timer step fires any pending timer (order nondeterministic, durations abstracted); GenServer {:noreply, s, t} as a self-timer that may fire even after a message arrived (sound over-approximation)
Model time explicitly with a clock and durations
Untimed timers: any pending timer may fire at any step; Process.exit(pid, r) queues an exit signal like a link would
Sys: timers list, Effect.sendAfter, Effect.signal, timerE step; extend supervisor/task proofs with the timer case
Timers and Effect.signal in Sys; SysStep.timer; both existing proofs extended with a 12-line frame case; all green first build

Watchdog example: pings a linked worker with a GenServer timeout, Process.exit(w, :kill) on timeout, restart on EXIT; translator: send to registered name, {:noreply, s, t}, Process.send_after, Process.exit, booleans

Watchdog translated (registered-name send, {:noreply,s,t}, Process.exit, booleans, named wildcards, pid-narrowed Option patterns, per-module catch-alls). Model check 10365 configs clean; no-trap mutant caught at 749; BEAM driver: hung worker killed by timeout, new worker running

BEAM subtlety the untimed model hides: any message resets a GenServer timeout, including :sys.get_state polls. The driver never saw the timeout until it stopped polling. In the model a timeout may fire regardless, which is the safe direction
nodes.description: Untimed timers over-approximate: the model admits a timeout firing after a pong. The real system under-fires when the mailbox is busy. Safety proofs hold in both; liveness of the watchdog (a hung worker is eventually replaced) would need the timer to actually fire, i.e. a fairness assumption on timers plus quiet mailboxes.

nodes.title: WatchdogProof: frame with child-preserving flag change, spawn shape with three effects, terminate_ne; signal/down/timer cases as before

Five translated examples cover the everyday BEAM toolbox: cast, call, reply, spawn/spawn_link, link, monitor, trap_exit, exit, Process.exit, send_after/timeouts. Each proof follows the frame+terminate recipe; the per-example novelty is one lemma

nodes.description: Substitute the init parameter(s) by the spawn-argument AST, then hand the bound expression to state_expr/4 in the parent's environment. Type-directed rendering works for both identity and non-identity init; the parent's own aliases (e.g. pid bound to fresh) still apply. Postwalk, not prewalk, so a substituted argument is not re-substituted.

init_of/2 accepted shapes: exactly one clause; body is {:ok, e} or block whose other stmts are all Process.flag(:trap_exit, true); e has no free vars beyond params and no self()
nodes.description: elixir/to_lean.exs init_of/2: collects def init(p) clauses from the module body; [] -> nil (identity default from use GenServer); more than one clause -> fail 'must have exactly one clause'. stmts(b) split into flags ++ [last]; each flag must be Process.flag(:trap_exit, true) else fail 'unsupported statement'; last must be {:ok, e} else fail 'must end in {:ok, state}'. free_vars(e) must all be in init_params(p) else fail 'state expression uses V, which is not a parameter'. A self() anywhere in e fails 'self() in the initial state is not supported'. The block form still marks the module as trapping (traps? is unchanged and independent).

nodes.title: child_state/6 binding: variable param -> whole spawn arg; 2-tuple or n-tuple param -> tuple literal positionally (mixed {a,b}/{:{},..} forms handled); nested tuple params deliberately unsupported
nodes.description: elixir/to_lean.exs child_state/6 pairs the init parameter pattern with the spawn argument AST: {v,_,nil} binds v to the whole arg; {a,b} vs {x,y}, {:{},_,ps} vs {:{},_,xs} of equal length, and the mixed 2/3-element tuple encodings zip positionally; anything else fails 'ParamPattern cannot be bound to spawn argument Arg'. Each bound param must itself be a bare variable (nested tuples like {{a,b},k} fail 'unsupported parameter pattern'). Then Macro.postwalk replaces each variable node in e by its bound arg and state_expr(env, bound, cctor, cfields) renders it in the parent env, so a parent pid aliased to fresh renders correctly. Scratch-tested (not committed): init({p,k}) -> {:ok,{p,k+1}} with {self(),0} gives .spawn (.worker me (0 + 1)), with {self(),r} gives .spawn (.worker me (r + 1)); block form with trap_exit gives .spawn (.worker me 7) and still traps.

Clause ordering in to_lean.exs ordered/1 + insert_crashes/2: per module cast/call clauses in source order, then crash clauses, then handle_info clauses; relative cast-vs-call order irrelevant under kind-disjoint-tags assumption
nodes.description: BEAM dispatch keys on the callback (handle_cast/handle_call/handle_info are separate functions) while the Lean beh is one match, so an info catch-all like '| _, _, .watchdog s_0 s_1, _ => ...' would shadow a crash clause if emitted first. ordered/1 splits a module's clauses into (cast|call) ++ info, each group in source order; insert_crashes/2 puts the crash clauses between the groups. A strict call-then-cast sort was rejected because Bank's generated file has handle_cast clauses before its handle_call clause and would no longer be byte-identical. classify/2 keys each {module, tag} by kind (every @type call alternative is a call tag even without a handle_call clause); a tag handled by two kinds is a hard fail('message tag ... handled by both ...'). Documented in the to_lean.exs header comment 'Unhandled messages (effects mode only)'. Visible effect in Gen/Watchdog.lean: the .pong clauses now precede the .start clause.

nodes.title: Totality (lean_total?/2, plain?/1) is judged on the rendered Lean pattern parts (env[:__mparts__]/[:__sparts__]), not on Elixir patterns, because pid-narrowing renders a bare w at pid()|nil as (some w)
nodes.description: lean_total? returns true iff the message pattern is bare or every rendered message part is a plain identifier, and every rendered state part is a plain identifier (none/true/false excluded). patterns/2 now stores the rendered message parts in env[:__mparts__]. Rationale from the builder: in watchdog.ex 'handle_cast(:pong, {w, true})' has state part (some w) and literal true, so it is not total and a crash clause for .pong is needed; judging on the Elixir AST would misclassify pid-narrowed variables as total (missing a crash clause) or literal-free-but-narrowed ones as partial (emitting a Lean-redundant clause that changes existing Gen files). A bare message variable in a cast/call clause covers every tag (:all in covered).

nodes.title: Two correctness changes riding on the new ordering: fallthrough/5 only searches same-kind clauses (a failed handle_cast guard no longer falls into a handle_info catch-all) and a bare cast/call pattern shadowing an info clause is now fail(...) instead of silently dropping it; also render/2 previously dropped ctx so warnings were never printed, now returns {string, ctx}
nodes.description: fallthrough/5 filter adds c.kind == cl.kind; when nothing matches and ctx.effects and the clause is cast/call the guard-failure result is '(state, [.exit .error])' (FunctionClauseError), otherwise the old warning 'guard has no fallthrough; Elixir would crash, modelled as no-op' remains for info clauses and message mode. render_clauses/2's subsumption check now fails with 'a <kind> clause of <mod> is shadowed by a bare <kind> pattern; use a tag' when the shadowing clause is of a different kind. main/1 destructures {out, ctx} = render(ctx, clauses) and prints ctx.warnings to stderr; before this the warnings list from render_clauses was discarded. No existing source hits any of these paths, so the five Gen files are unchanged.

Defer clause and loop_tail semantics: a loop module with no unguarded bare-pattern clause gets '| me, _, .<mod> s_0.., m => (.<mod> s_0.., [.send me m])' after its last clause; tail 'f(e)' -> {:noreply, e}, 'exit(r)' kept, statement kept then exit(:normal), plain value -> exit(:normal); rewriting descends through if/case
nodes.description: elixir/to_lean.exs: defers = loop modules with no clause where guard == nil and bare?(mpat). render_clauses/2 tags each rendered clause with its module, finds the module's last clause index and appends defer_clause(ctx, mod) right after it; the module ctor is then added to ctx.covered so no global catch-all is emitted (Gen/Supervisor.lean lost '| _, _, s, _ => (s, [])'). loop_tail/2 recurses into {:if, ..} and {:case, ..} branches; on a block it splits off the last statement: {^fname, _, [e]} -> {:noreply, e}; {:exit, _, [_]} kept; otherwise value?(last) (atom/int/list/var/tuple) drops the value and appends exit(:normal), a non-value statement is kept and followed by exit(:normal). Why it matters: this is the encoding of selective receive; the re-enqueue delivers to self, so the message count of the process is preserved and the proof must frame it (mcount_deliver). The explorer never sends start/EXIT to a worker, so the defer clause does not enlarge the explored state space; it is exercised by beh_eq_gen and the SupervisorProof cases, not by the checker.

nodes.title: Guard failure in a defer module: a guarded receive clause with no more-general later clause re-enqueues instead of the GenServer no-op; fallthrough/5 returns deferred=true, header becomes '| me, _, sp, m@(.pat)' (m' if the clause binds m), and no 'guard has no fallthrough' warning is emitted
nodes.description: elixir/to_lean.exs fallthrough/5 now returns {rhs, ctx, deferred}. When no later clause of the same module is at least as general: if cl.mod in ctx.defers the fallback is '(sp, [.send me <msg_name>])' and deferred=true, else the old behaviour (warning 'clause i guard has no fallthrough; Elixir would crash, modelled as no-op' and '(sp, [])'). In render_clauses/2 a deferred clause names the whole message with an as-pattern msg_name(env)@(mp) and forces the self name to 'me' (self_name(env) might be '_'). msg_name/1 picks m' when the clause already binds a variable m. This matches BEAM semantics: a receive arm whose guard fails does not consume the message. Verified by the builder only on an uncommitted scratch module (no committed example exercises a guarded receive clause).

nodes.title: Limitations of loop_of/1 and spawn mapping: exactly one loop per module, one parameter, no guard on the head, no 'after'; mixing with handle_* fails; a loop module always switches on effects mode; spawn requires :f to be Mod's loop fn (Map.get(c.loops, child) == fname); spawn_monitor lhs must be {pid, _ref}; spawn forms bind pid via bind_fresh/2 shared with GenServer.start_link
nodes.description: elixir/to_lean.exs loop_of/1 matches {:def, _, [head, [do: {:receive, _, [opts]}]]}: the def body must be exactly one receive (no statements before it); [do: arms] only, so 'after' clauses fail with 'receive loop f must take one argument and have no guard or after'; more than one loop fails; handle_cast/handle_info/handle_call alongside a loop fails 'a module cannot mix GenServer callbacks with a receive loop'. Bodies with other receives (nested receive inside an arm, or receive in helper functions) are not detected as loops. sends/3 spawn case: {:=, _, [lhs, {f, _, [{:__aliases__,_,[child]}, fname, [arg]]}]} with f in spawn/spawn_link/spawn_monitor; the spawned function must be the target module's loop, so spawning a GenServer module via spawn_link(Mod, :init, ..) is rejected; bare spawn without a binding is not recognised (falls through to the default statement handling). effects_in?/spawns? recognise 3-arity spawn calls only. Builder verified guarded defer, spawn, spawn_monitor, statement tail and if-in-tail on a scratch module that was not committed; those paths have no regression test in the repo.

nodes.description: Scratch file combo.ex (Worker raw loop with :job/{:set,k} when k>0/:crash/:stop; Sup GenServer with init(n) trap_exit block, handle_info :start spawn_link + EXIT, handle_cast :restart on nil-child state and {:kick,k} when k>n). Output ordering per module: worker arms, worker defer clause; sup .restart, .kick, crash clause for .restart, then .start and .EXIT info clauses; global catch-all kept because Sup is not covered. The pre-existing 'clause 7 guard has no fallthrough' warning is the info-clause EXIT pid-narrowing guard, as at base. No committed example exercises guarded defer or spawn_monitor; adding one would give these paths a regression test.
